items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: the Scottish saxophone player who I’ve played with, Raymond MacDonald

ctx.x: Well you said you played for the dance classes and I’m wondering if you took some of those drawings, those abstract drawings and picked one out and put it on the piano in front of you, could you play the drawing?

Yeah. I could. In fact, a few years ago some Scottish musicians and artists and some American musicians and I did a joint project here in Woodstock. We had an exhibition where we collaborated on the artwork and the music, we created these graphic scores. The Scottish artist whose name Jo Ganter, Josephine Ganter, and she created a lot of grid patterns and over those I drew some things and then the Scottish saxophone player who I’ve played with, Raymond MacDonald, he did other kinds of things on top of those grid

patterns. He filled them in with different colors and things so they were very different. And we had this whole exhibition of graphic scores, we wrote instructions of how they were to be played and went in the studio, I went in the studio and recorded a series of the ones that I had done with David Rothenberg who played clarinet and laptop electronics, and then these were all up on the wall with headphones so people could listen to the music we recorded to each one, each drawing, and then Jo created animations of…
